chunks: It was narrated from Murazim ibn Hakim Al-Azdi from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him): Regarding the infant when he is circumcised,

He said: 'One should say: O Allah, this is Your Sunnah and the Sunnah of Your Prophet, may Your prayers be upon him and his family, and it is our following of You and Your Prophet by Your will, Your desire, and Your decree for a matter You have willed, a decision You have made obligatory, and a command You have executed, so You made him taste the heat of iron in his circumcision and cupping for a matter You know better than I do. O Allah, purify him from sins, increase his lifespan, protect his body from afflictions and his flesh from pain, increase him in wealth, and remove poverty from him. Indeed, You know while we do not.'

Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) also said: 'Whoever does not say this at the time of his child's circumcision should say it for him before he reaches puberty. If he says it, he will be protected from the heat of iron, whether from killing or anything else.'

key_terms.حَرَّ الْحَدِيد: Heat of iron (metaphor for pain or hardship)

ai.seo_question: What is the recommended supplication for a child's circumcision in Shia tradition?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq records this supplication from Imam al-Sadiq (AS), framing circumcision not merely as a physical act but as an emulation of the Prophet’s Sunnah and a submission to divine decree (Qada). The text highlights the spiritual efficacy of this specific prayer, promising that reciting it before puberty shields the child from the 'heat of iron,' a metaphor for various trials, hardships, or premature death, thereby linking ritual practice to divine protection.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.4726 - It was narrated from Murazim ibn Hakim Al-Azdi that Abu Abdullah (as) said regarding the circumcision of a child:

"One should say:
O Allah (swt), this is Your (swt) Sunnah and the Sunnah of Your Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him and his family), and it is our following of You (swt) and Your Prophet (sw) by Your (swt) will, Your (swt) desire, and Your (swt) decree for a matter You (swt) have willed, a decision You (swt) have made obligatory, and a command You (swt) have executed.
You (swt) have made him taste the heat of iron in his circumcision and cupping for a matter You (swt) know better than I do. O Allah (swt), purify him from sins, increase his lifespan, protect his body from afflictions and his flesh from pain, increase him in wealth, and remove poverty from him. Indeed, You (swt) know while we do not."

Abu Abdullah (as) also said: "Whoever does not say this at the time of his child's circumcision should say it before the child reaches puberty. If he says it, the child will be protected from the heat of iron, whether from killing or anything else."
